general.bannerDescription: Wide cover image for the home page and the instance header. PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MB – or use one of your own in the “Screenshots” tab.
general.groupDescription: Groups organize the instances in your library. An instance belongs to at most one group.
general.channelDescription: Which versions “Update” and “latest compatible version” pick.
general.duplicateDescription: Creates a copy with all worlds, mods and settings – handy before changing versions.
general.exportDescription: Writes an .mrpack file for sharing or backing up. Mods from Modrinth are linked instead of copied.
general.deleteDescription: Permanently deletes the instance with all its worlds, mods and screenshots.

installation.changeHint: Worlds and settings are kept when you switch; mods installed from Modrinth or CurseForge can then be updated to compatible versions. Worlds are converted on first launch – to be safe, duplicate the instance first.
installation.boostDescription: Runs the instance with Fabric, the TRS Client and performance mods like Sodium under the hood – a lot more FPS. Off = pure vanilla.
installation.clientDescription: HUD with FPS, CPS, keystrokes and ping, zoom (V) and fullbright. Open the in-game menu with Right Shift.
installation.repairDescription: Checks every game file by checksum and re-downloads damaged ones. Worlds and mods are left untouched.
installation.reinstallDescription: Downloads the game version, mod loader and libraries again from scratch. Worlds, mods and settings are kept.
installation.reinstallConfirmText: The game version and libraries will be downloaded again. Worlds, mods and settings are kept.
installation.tuningDescription: Tuned Java settings for more FPS and fewer stutters. Custom JVM arguments take priority.
installation.fpsModeDescription: How the TRS Client sets up the video options and performance mods. Pretty keeps the look and only uses performance switches; Max FPS turns off clouds, smooth lighting and fancy leaves. Applied at the next start; your own changes stay.

hooks.intro: Commands run through {cmd} without a window, for at most 2 minutes. Available: {id}, {name}, {dir}, {mcDir} and {java}.
hooks.preLaunchDescription: Runs before the game starts. If it fails, the game won't start.
hooks.wrapperDescription: Put in front of the Java command line, e.g. a profiler or launcher.
hooks.postExitDescription: Runs after the game has closed. Errors show up as a notice.

sync.intro: Items turned on globally are fetched from shared storage before launch and written back after the game closes. Here you can keep them separate for this instance. Overwritten files are backed up first.
sync.globallyOff: Turned off globally – turn it on in Settings under Instances.

appearance.accentDescription: Color for buttons, active items and the redstone wire.
appearance.advancedRenderingDescription: Blur effects behind dialogs and bars. Turning it off saves a little performance on slower PCs.
appearance.animatedBackgroundDescription: A calm redstone circuit behind every page. When off, only the deepslate pattern is shown.

behavior.title: Behavior
behavior.closeOnLaunchTitle: Minimize launcher when the game starts
behavior.closeOnLaunchDescription: The window gets out of the way on launch; the game keeps running even if you close the launcher.
behavior.compactLibraryDescription: Smaller tiles – more instances at a glance.
behavior.showPlayTimeDescription: Total play time on tiles and instance pages.
behavior.showSnapshotsDescription: Include snapshots and old versions in the version picker by default.
behavior.restartOnboardingDescription: Walks you through signing in and your first instance once more.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.logUploadDescription: “Share log” uploads the game log to mclo.gs – credentials and username are redacted first. When off, the button doesn't work.
privacy.discordDescription: Your Discord profile shows “Playing TRS Launcher” – while you play, also the Minecraft version, mod loader and play time. Never server addresses, instance or player names. The launcher only talks to the Discord app on this PC.
privacy.telemetryDescription: TRS Launcher doesn't collect any usage or crash data. There's nothing to turn on.

defaults.title: Defaults for all instances
defaults.hint: Instances can override individual values in their own settings.
defaults.memoryDescription: The maximum amount of RAM the game may use.
defaults.minMemoryDescription: Initial value for Java (-Xms), in MB.
defaults.envDescription: Apply to the game and the launch hooks.
defaults.resolutionDescription: Width × height of the game window.
defaults.dedicatedGpuDescription: Minecraft uses the dedicated graphics card (important on laptops). Only applies to the launcher’s own Java and is undone when you switch it off.
defaults.tuningDescription: Tuned Java settings for your Java version and memory (G1, from 12 GB ZGC; memory reserved up front). Your own JVM arguments win where they overlap.
defaults.priorityDescription: Starts the game with the priority “Above normal” – can smooth out stutters while other programs are busy.
defaults.dedicatedGpuDescriptionLinux: For laptops with two graphics chips: the game renders on the dedicated GPU (PRIME offload – DRI_PRIME or the NVIDIA variables).

hooks.title: Launch hooks
hooks.preLaunchDescription: Runs via cmd /C before every launch; if it fails, the game doesn't start.
hooks.wrapperDescription: Placed in front of the Java command line.
hooks.postExitDescription: Runs after the game has closed.

sync.title: Sync
sync.description: Anything turned on is fetched from shared storage before launch and written back after exit – so every instance has the same settings. The first instance that has a file provides the starting point; overwritten files are backed up.

java.title: Java installations
java.hint: Empty = the launcher automatically installs the right Java version from Mojang.
java.globalDescription: Only needed if a single Java should be used for everything – the entries above take priority.

storage.title: Storage
storage.verifyDescription: Checks the shared game files by checksum. Damaged files are removed and downloaded again on the next launch.
storage.verifyRemoved: {checked} files checked, {removed} damaged removed – they'll be downloaded again on the next launch.
storage.cleanDescription: {n} game version isn't needed by any instance anymore ({size}). It will be downloaded again if needed. | {n} game versions aren't needed by any instance anymore ({size}). They will be downloaded again if needed.
storage.cleanDescriptionEmpty: Game versions that no instance needs anymore.
storage.confirmText: {n} game version ({size}) will be deleted. Instances, worlds and mods stay untouched. | {n} game versions ({size}) will be deleted. Instances, worlds and mods stay untouched.
storage.credentialsKeyring: The key for your Microsoft sign-ins is kept in your system keyring (e.g. GNOME Keyring or KWallet).
storage.credentialsFile: No system keyring was found, so your sign-ins are only protected by file permissions (only your user can read them). Install and unlock a keyring such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet for better protection.

network.title: Network
network.autoFirewallDescription: Otherwise Windows asks for every single Java version whether Minecraft may access the network (e.g. for LAN worlds). New Java versions are allowed before launch with one admin prompt.
network.firewallDescription: Adds the rule for all of the launcher's Java versions at once – a single admin prompt.
network.allowed: Network access allowed for {n} Java program | Network access allowed for {n} Java programs
network.downloadsDescription: How many files are downloaded at the same time. Use fewer on a slow connection.

clips.title: Clips & recording
clips.intro: Like ShadowPlay or Medal: the launcher records only the game window while a game from this launcher runs. Everything stays on your PC.
clips.enabledDescription: Keeps the last seconds in a buffer on disk so a key press saves them as a clip. Off by default.
clips.ffmpegMissing: Downloaded once when you turn clips on ({size}, checksum verified).
clips.bufferDescription: How many seconds a clip goes back.
clips.resolutionDescription: Larger game windows are scaled down.
clips.encoderDescription: Automatic uses your graphics card (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) and falls back to software.
clips.systemAudioDescription: Records what your speakers play (game, music, voice chat).
clips.microphoneDescription: Adds your default microphone. Off by default.
clips.limitDescription: Above this size the oldest clips are moved to the recycle bin.
clips.keysText: F9 saves a clip, F10 starts and stops a recording. Change them in the Minecraft controls under “TRS Client”.
clips.privacy: Nothing leaves your PC: no upload, no account, the recorder only runs while a game from this launcher is open.

trsConsent.title: Use TRS services?
trsConsent.intro: With TRS services you get {capes}, a {friendsList} with online status, and you can follow friends onto their server. To do this, the launcher signs in to the TRS server ({host}) with your Minecraft account – just like joining a Minecraft server. The server never gets your password or your Minecraft token.
